subject: Help with CSS (to be used with knitr::spin() )

messages.author: 4f6f5f995ee31178
messages.subject: Help with CSS (to be used with knitr::spin() )
parts:
Hi!

I'm very happy with the html pages I'm getting using spin() out
of minimally tuned R scripts. It is more than I actually had thought I could
do to get a good documentation of my work. Thanks a lot to the developer(s).

Few details remain to get the resulting html  with a bit more of style. I think
(according to https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/knitr/wyqwR1Uc29Q)
that customizing my markdown.css should be the way, but I find the doc a bit overwhelming.
I'd appreciate help/suggestions on:

1. How to define a fixed page width, i.e. such as in
http://nsaunders.wordpress.com/2012/08/27/custom-css-for-html-generated-using-rstudio/
Actually, that page is great help for making nice tables but does not tell how to
get the style of the actual page.
I understand there is nothing I have to do "at the spin() level" (nothing to include in the actual
R script to be run by spin()) but just modify my css and use
 markdownToHTML(inputFile, outputFile, stylesheet='custom.css') 
as explained in 
http://www.rstudio.com/ide/docs/authoring/markdown_custom_rendering

but do not really know what to include in the css to get such a nice page format.

2. How to include the TOC. I've found this advice:
library(knitr)
knit2html('foo.Rmd', options = c('toc', markdown::markdownHTMLOptions(TRUE)))

but is it correct to mix markdownToHTML() and knit2html()?

Thanks

Agus

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Help with CSS (to be used with knitr::spin() )
parts:
2. knit2html() calls markdownToHTML(), and any additional arguments
passed to the former are passed to the latter, so it is okay to pass
the `options` argument;

1. see above; also note markdownToHTML() has a 'header' argument,
which can take additional HTML headers; for your case, you can take a
look at https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/misc/vignette.css
as an example

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Help with CSS (to be used with knitr::spin() )
parts:
Thanks,
I've included the settings for tables indicated in
http://nsaunders.wordpress.com/2012/08/27/custom-css-for-html-generated-using-rstudio/
and the general ones from yours in
https://github.com/yihui/knitr/blob/master/inst/misc/vignette.css
with slight modifications within the markdown.css file of RStudio
to create an alternative custom.css

What I do is:
require(knitr)
require(markdown)
spin("myscript.R")
markdowToHTML("myscript.md", "myscript.html", stylesheet='custom.css')

Just 2 minor problems
1. I do not find the way to set the option "stylesheet=" for markdown
within spin(). If it were possible, I could just run, i.e.
spin("myscript.R", stylesheet='custom.css')

2. I've tried to set a color for the background but just for the width defined here:
body{width:800px;margin:auto;background-color:#EDEDED}
but I get all the page (not only the 800px) with color #EDEDED

Thanks a lot for this impressive tool. You get so much out of spin() with so few added codes.

Agus
